lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1731 — sorted by where it goes, and the vendor admits what you own

Both of your asks. The second one turned out to have a dead message behind it.

── 1. ARMOR AND JEWELLERY DIVIDE BY BODY PART ──────────────────────────────

*"armor should also be split up into subcategories like the weapons, but just by
what part of the body it is for, same as for the rings/amulets category."*

    ARMOR                 AMULETS & RINGS
      HEAD · n              AMULETS · n
      CHEST · n             RINGS · n
      HANDS · n
      LEGS · n
      FEET · n
      CLOAKS · n

⚠⚠ THE MECHANISM WAS REUSED, NOT COPIED. OTA-1683 already built labelled runs
inside a section for Weapons. The screen carried
`cat === 'weapon' ? weaponRuns(...) : [one unlabelled run]` inline — adding two
more dividing categories there would have been three special cases in a render
body. That ternary is now one `categoryRuns(cat, items)`, so the screen asks one
question and a fourth category later cannot mean a fourth branch.

⚠⚠⚠ THE AUTHORITY IS `validSlotsForItem`, and that is the point rather than a
convenience. It is the SAME function `slotFillLabelFor` already calls to print
"Head" / "Chest" on the row itself, and the one the equip router obeys — so a
subsection heading can never disagree with the rows under it, and can never claim
a slot the game will not actually put the piece in. It also resolves FUSED pieces
off `uniqueStats` (OTA-224) instead of a name lookup that misses them entirely.

⚠ MEASURED BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN, because a heading nothing lands under is
worse than no heading:

    297 armour rows ....  head 77 · chest 60 · cloak 43 · hands 41 · feet 39 · legs 37
     48 accessories ....  ring 28 · amulet 20
    rows that fail to resolve to a slot ......... 0

There is no "Other" bucket in the data. One exists in the code anyway, so a fused
oddity or a future authored row stays REACHABLE instead of falling out of the list
because it did not fit a heading.

⚠ A SECTION WITH ONLY ONE KIND IN IT GETS NO SUB-HEADING. Three helms under a
heading reading "HEAD" inside a section already titled ARMOR is a label repeating
its own parent.

── 2. THE VENDOR ADMITS WHAT YOU ALREADY OWN ───────────────────────────────

*"ensure that if I have already bought a 'working to learn' I can see that I own
it if someone tries to sell it to me again."*

⚠⚠ THE ROW VANISHED. Three workings became two, and an ABSENCE had to carry the
meaning "you own this" — which no absence can. You could not tell whether the
trader never stocked it or whether it was already in your book.

⚠ THE VENDOR GENUINELY STILL HAS IT, and that is OTA-802's design working
correctly: a vendor's menu is a FIXED seeded slice of the full discoverable pool
so it cannot reroll ("learning one just drops it, the rest keep their identity").
The stock was right; only the display was lying by omission. The row stays now and
reads ✓ KNOWN in completion-green, greyed, and NOT tappable — tapping would open a
confirm sheet for a purchase the store then refuses, which is the dead-control
defect OTA-220 rules out.

⚠⚠ ONE SLICE, TWO VIEWS. `vendorRecipeMenu` computes the three rows and marks the
owned ones; `vendorRecipeOffers` is now DERIVED from it as "the menu minus what you
know" — byte-identical output to what it always returned, so every existing caller
and OTA-802's stability contract are untouched, and "which three" has exactly one
answer instead of the slice arithmetic existing twice. The screen's own duplicate
`.filter` on knownRecipes went with it: it re-applied a rule the engine had already
applied, which is how the shelf and the display ended up with two opinions.

⚠⚠⚠ AND IT MADE A DEAD MESSAGE LIVE. `buyFromVendor` looks the typed name up in
the recipe list and then checks `knownRecipes.includes(...)` to say

    "You already know the Hearty Stew working."

It was reading `vendorRecipeOffers`, which has ALREADY dropped everything you know
— so that branch could never be true. Typing the name of a working you own fell
through to the ordinary item lookup and answered *"doesn't carry any Hearty Stew"*,
which is the exact opposite of the truth: they carry it, you own it. It reads the
MENU now, so the message the game already had can finally be said.

── ONE EXISTING PIN RE-POINTED, AND ITS CLAIM NARROWED ─────────────────────

OTA-1683's suite pinned the literal ternary, and its title read "…and every other
section is one unlabelled run". That second half is no longer true. Re-pointing the
string alone would have left a test asserting a sentence the game had stopped
meaning, so the title and the assertions now state the property OTA-1683 actually
cared about — Weapons render in labelled runs, a section with nothing to divide
renders as one unlabelled run — checked against `categoryRuns` itself rather than
against a source literal.

11 tests including a REAL RENDER that opens both sections and reads all six body
headings plus Amulets and Rings off the tree. 19 gates green, complete surface
clean.
